faq.question: What is Google Security Checkup?
faq.answer: It's a free page in your Google account (myaccount.google.com/security-checkup) that reviews your security in one place: saved passwords, signed-in devices, recent security activity, recovery options, two-step verification and apps with access to your account. It flags issues by colour, from red for urgent to blue for tips.

faq.question: What does "compromised password" mean in Google?
faq.answer: One of your saved passwords has been found in a data breach on another website. Change it on that site immediately, and on any other site where you used the same password.

faq.question: Should I remove third-party access from my Google account?
faq.answer: Remove any app or website you don't recognise or no longer use. Removing access doesn't delete your account with that service; it just stops it reading your Google data, and you can sign in again later if needed.

faq.question: What should I do if I see a sign-in I don't recognise?
faq.answer: Change your Google password, sign out the unknown device, check that your recovery phone and email haven't been changed, look for unfamiliar Gmail forwarding rules or filters, and turn on 2-Step Verification.

faq.question: Is Enhanced Safe Browsing worth turning on?
faq.answer: For most people, yes. It checks websites and downloads with Google in real time and, according to Google, makes users twice as safe from phishing as Standard protection. The trade-off is that more browsing data is sent to Google for checking.
